findings.summary: Section 6's criterion remains unmet: one promoted claim outlives its worker.
findings.text: The record's own verdict is that section 6's criterion is unmet: at the six-hour census one promoted claim (r-20261120T074437034953-cym-s5, 2.2 d old, no turn in progress, liveness dead) still holds a pointer, because the compare-under-lock equality accepts 1 of 94 pointers and rejects 93. The deliverable reports a failed measure rather than a passed one; the cause sits in the release module's equality (outside this node's declared write path), so it needs its own node rather than a repair here.

findings.summary: The 'before' census is 26 minutes after the last landing, not before it.
findings.text: The done_when asks for a census taken before the release work landed. The record's first census was taken at 2026-11-22T09:38:51Z, twenty-six minutes after the last landing at 09:12:18Z, because the landings predated dispatch; the record states this plainly and names the three section-1 kinds that had no pointer that day, which is the fallback the done_when allows.

findings.summary: The gate checks links, not the census measure the done_when asserts.
findings.text: The run's recorded gate is `reckon audit-doc ... --check-links`, which validates document structure and links only. No check in the run asserts the census counts (76/76, 94/94), the equality reading (1 of 94) or the residual-claim count, so a record whose numbers regressed could still pass the gate; the base arm is 'FILE ABSENT' with EXIT=1 rather than a failing assertion, so the delta of added failures is 0 by construction.

findings.summary: Census counts are self-reported by the instrument with no external control.
findings.text: The headline figures are reported by the census instrument itself and are not independently re-derivable after the fact: the live directory has moved on since 15:21:52Z, and the record's only cross-check on the read count is arithmetic from the same reading (94 pointers + 19 non-pointers = 113 entries). The instrument does read the directory entry count back and refuses on any unread pointer, which is the check the done_when names, but it is not an external control.
